pr_title: [Fix #9328] Recognize shareable_constant_value magic comment in Style/MutableConstant
pr_body:
Ruby 3.0 adds `shareable_constant_value` magic comment. This PR changes `Style/MutableConstant` to be aware of `shareable_constant_value` magic comment.

Fixes #9328.

-----------------

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] The PR relates to *only* one subject with a clear title and description in grammatically correct, complete sentences.
* [x] Wrote [good commit messages][1].
* [x] Commit message starts with `[Fix #issue-number]` (if the related issue exists).
* [x] Feature branch is up-to-date with `master` (if not - rebase it).
* [x] Squashed related commits together.
* [x] Added tests.
* [x] Ran `bundle exec rake default`. It executes all tests and runs RuboCop on its own code.
* [x] Added an entry (file) to the [changelog folder](https://github.com/rubocop-hq/rubocop/blob/master/changelog/) named `{change_type}_{change_description}.md` if the new code introduces user-observable changes. See [changelog entry format](https://github.com/rubocop-hq/rubocop/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entry-format) for details.

[1]: https://chris.beams.io/posts/git-commit/
pr_comments:
I can't have a thorough look right now, but `shareable_constant_value` is tricky, because it can change only part of the code. Does this PR handle this?
```ruby
# shareable_constant_value: literal
X = [1, 2, 3]
# shareable_constant_value: false
Y = [1, 2, 3]
```

And raise on offense for `Y` and none for `X`?

> And raise on offense for Y and none for X?

Yes. X is tested in https://github.com/rubocop-hq/rubocop/pull/9410/files#diff-6e9b3e5cdbc957813be5790f5b8c0850c30c3f1bf0eef7576009023cad7c3f25R160. I'll add a test for Y on ruby 3.0.
Closing in favour of #9929 that builds on top of this PR.

issue_context.title: `Style/MutableConstant` should be aware of `# shareable_constant_value` (Ruby 3.0)
issue_context.body:
The following should not generate an offense:

```ruby
# shareable_constant_value: literal (or experimental_everything)

MY_CONSTANT = %w[anything here is fine even non-literals]
```
comments:
Here's a link to some documentation on the feature, https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/3.0.0/doc/syntax/comments_rdoc.html#label-shareable_constant_value+Directive. 

https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/17273

I hadn't heard of this being added before so I found it to be an interesting feature. It seems like the intent is to be used with Ractors

>  It seems like the intent is to be used with Ractors

That's one way to view it. The other way is the general position that constants should be immutable, and clearly when we say that we never mean actual classes. So in effect that is pretty much what "Ractor-shareable" means.
I created https://github.com/rubocop-hq/rubocop/pull/9410 to recognize shareable_constant_value in Style/MutableConstant

review_comments: I find it surprising that the tests started failing when i changed `immutable_literal?(value)` to `!mutable_literal?(value)`.
This had to be split into 2 lines because of line length, but it makes the magic comment less readable. 🤔
